Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing RS Carbon Fiber Edition Rocks No Less Than 968 Horsepower and Subdued Looks
14 photos
Photo: roadshowinternational / Instagram
Cadillac hasn’t done much lately because it’s busy trying to figure out a way to reverse the recent sales slump caused by its over-reliance on all-electric models that aren’t selling great in America anymore.
Well, they have things to do, for sure: General Motors hinted that although the CT4 will be retired this year, the larger CT5 will soldier on, and its platform and production location will even be shared with an upcoming Buick passenger car along with the returning Chevrolet Camaro.
Additionally, although Cadillac ended XT6 production back in 2025, it’s now considering bringing it back as it renews its interest in combustion-powered models. The mid-size luxury crossover SUV with three-row seating produced for the 2020 to 2025 model years for North America is another sign that Cadillac is reversing course on EVs, and the brand officially revealed the nameplate will make a return to the model lineup.
Basically, it will be a new three-row crossover SUV that’s neither electric nor body-on-frame like the Escalade . So, in the near future, there are good prospects for a Caddy rebound. Until then, all we can do to support them is to showcase their coolest models – including from across the aftermarket realm.
For example, the good folks over at Atlanta, Georgia-based Road Show International have another treat “for the culture” that has reached the “sold” RS Edition status – a Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing RS
Carbon Fiber Edition that’s dressed completely in black except for the badges, so it’s not actually ‘murdered-out.’ Also, it’s not very obvious, either.
Well, at least at first look – because if you pay attention, you’ll notice there’s a ton of aftermarket goodies on top of the already cool factory package. According to the dealership, their newly sold Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing RS Carbon Fiber Edition is dressed in Black with a Black and Ivory interior that also has loads of carbon fiber and some nice red accents here and there.
The rather inconspicuous executive performance sedan is actually capable of shaming supercars now, as the company says it has 968 hp and 859 lb-ft of torque thanks to their RS Performance Package bringing an additional 300 hp and 200 WTQ, and it also rides on massive 21-inch front and 22-inch rear staggered Black and Carbon Fiber wheels to reach 62 mph in 2.8 seconds and a top speed of no less than 200 mph.
Additionally, the RS Edition includes a complete music and lighting package, a full vehicle paint protection film (PPF) wrap, nano-ceramic window and windshield tint, a two-tone tag gloss frame, as well as ceramic paint coating protection. So, what do you think – is this thing cool or way too inconspicuous? View this post on Instagram A post shared by ROAD SHOW INTERNATIONAL (@roadshowinternational)
